flags.message: The manifest marks the 140-page petition truncated. The QP, main argument, and reproduced decision under review are usable, but completeness of the remaining appendix and trial-record material cannot be assumed. No BIO is provisioned, consistently with the respondent's waiver. Prediction completed with these limitations; no case outcome was retrieved.

The frozen band is `baseline` (sal-v4) although the snapshot already shows the two strongest cert-stage signals this docket carries: a Court-requested response (Sep 29 2026, after the government waived) and ten amicus briefs at the cert stage. Neither signal is a band input or a statpack cut, so the scored yardstick for this cell (the baseline band's bracketed reached rate, about 5% pooled over OT2017-OT2025) understates the population this petition actually sits in. I anchored on the band as instructed and adjusted upward from the record; noting it here because a response-requested cut (and an amicus-count cut) on the paid scored segment would make cells like this one scoreable against the right population.

Forward-mode companion signal, disclosed as hygiene: the Sixth Circuit companion petition Ream v. Department of the Treasury (No. 26-93) was fetched from supremecourt.gov and shows it was rescheduled off the 9/28 conference and re-distributed for the same 10/9/2026 conference as this petition, with eleven amicus entries. This public, pre-snapshot information about a different docket raised my grant probability; it reveals nothing about this case's own disposition, which does not yet exist.

Forward cell ran on 2026-10-04 for a petition first distributed for the 2026-09-28 long conference; a corpus priors query showed other petitions from that conference with cert grants dated 2026-10-01, so the conference's grant list had already issued when this cell ran. I did not retrieve this docket's post-conference state or disposition and forecast from the provisioned baseline (one distribution, no CVSG) only. Flagging so the evaluator can weigh the vantage; no leakage occurred.

The provisioned record has no documents directory, petition, opposition, or QP text. I recovered the pre-grant lower-court opinion and official QP from court hosts, but did not obtain the parties' cert briefs or the correspondence mentioned in the snapshot. This is an input-coverage limitation, not a missing filing or a known provisioning violation; the completed forecast discounts confidence accordingly.

No record/documents/ directory (and no documents.json) was provisioned for this merits grant-moment cell although the petition, QP, and BIO are public on supremecourt.gov; the snapshot even carries a QPLink. I retrieved the QP and the government's petition (with the Second Circuit opinion appended) myself in forward mode. Not a blocker, but the cell forecast from retrieved rather than provisioned filings, so predictors in this fan-out may not share the same document baseline.

Vehicle note for the evaluator: the government filed No. 26-104 as a hold petition asking the Court to hold it behind Putra v. Lopez-Campos (No. 25-1415, CA6), yet the October 1 order granted only 26-104 and left 25-1415 and Buenrostro-Mendez (No. 26-43, CA5) undisposed. The forecast treats that vehicle choice as a modest signal; it is pre-decision public information, not outcome material.

The event declares moment distribution, but context supplies snapshot_provenance as-stored with null cutoff and cut_kind. The October 4 snapshot includes September 12 filings after the September 9 first distribution. Used the supplied record under the forward-mode contract; this forecast should not be interpreted as verified conditioning strictly at first distribution. No disposition of the target cert petition was encountered; the recorded stay denials concern a separate application.

Forward cell run on 2026-10-04 for a petition distributed to the 9/28/2026 long conference. A fedcourts query for recent priors returned another OT2026 paid petition (26-104) from the same conference already recorded as granted, so the long-conference grant orders have issued and this petition was not among them. This is public calendar context predating the snapshot, not this case's disposition (which I did not retrieve and do not know); it lowered my relist-increment claim and left the grant number essentially unchanged.
record/documents/application.txt was provisioned with empty_text: true (scanned 24-page stay application, no text layer). Treated as content-unavailable; nothing inferred from it.

No petition, questions-presented text, BIO, lower-court reasoning, or documents manifest was provisioned. The snapshot describes paper-only filing and supplies no petition link. Forecast completed from the procedural snapshot and committed prior-Term rates; substantive certworthiness remains unassessed and big_case_score is explicitly null. This is an input limitation, not a finding that the petition lacks a substantial question.

The provisioned petition is readable and untruncated, but its separately linked appendix and the underlying Arizona memorandum decision are not provisioned. The core grant theory depends on their treatment of waiver, notice, and missing transcripts. Those characterizations remain petitioner's allegations, not independently verified findings. No brief in opposition is provisioned. Prediction completed from the supplied record and prior-Term base rates without seeking the case's outcome.

Hold petition: the QP states it presents the same question as No. 25-1383 (Indian Harbor v. Town of Vinton) and asks the Court to hold it. The forecast is therefore driven by Vinton's docket (response requested Jul 27 2026 after a waiver; two cert-stage amici; no redistribution or disposition as of Oct 4 2026), read from supremecourt.gov because the corpus does not track 25-1383 (no scotus/9025001383 case). The Aug 27 'Rescheduled' entry here tracks Vinton rather than signalling anything about this petition's own merits; resolution may take until mid-2027 if Vinton is granted.

The briefed moment appears to fire on a respondent aligned in partial support of petitioner, not completion of adversarial merits briefing. The August 28 merits-brief-respondent.txt is Arizona and its Attorney General's partial-support brief; it agrees on the state-form statutory issue, contests the decree issue, and expressly does not discuss question two. The snapshot's July 20 order sets opposing respondents' briefs for October 13, 2026. Forecast completed using the actual partial-support brief and retained truncated cert-stage opposition, without assuming opposing merits briefing exists. Consider alignment-aware moment detection and document selection.

The `briefed` moment opened on 2026-08-28, but every respondent brief filed that day is aligned with the petitioner: the United States in support, the Arizona legislative leaders in support, and the State of Arizona in partial support. The adverse respondents' (Mi Familia Vota, DNC, AANHPI coalition) merits briefs are due 2026-10-13 per the docket. So 'both sides' merits briefs are on the record' is not true at this cutoff; the cell is effectively a petitioner-briefed moment. The event minter may want to key on an adverse respondent's brief (or the first brief filed after the respondents' due date) when the docket shows multi-sided respondents.

`merits-brief-respondent.txt` is the State of Arizona and Attorney General's brief in partial support of petitioner (it argues the NVRA question for the petitioner and defends only the consent-decree holding). It is labeled as the respondent's merits brief in documents.json. The United States' and the legislative leaders' August 28 briefs were not provisioned (one row per side). I read Arizona's brief as what it is and did not treat it as the opposition.

My adjustment above the merits base rate leans on two public, pre-snapshot Supreme Court stay orders that I know from the filings and from training: the partial stay in this case (24A164, Aug. 2024) and Beals v. Virginia Coalition for Immigrant Rights (Oct. 2024). Both predate the snapshot and are cited in the petition and BIOs; noted for hygiene, not as leakage.

Forward merits cell. Open-web retrieval (SCOTUSblog case page, the supremecourt.gov docket page, and the SG's CVSG brief PDF on justice.gov) surfaced public material postdating the 2026-08-18 baseline: the United States filed a merits amicus brief in support of respondents on 2026-08-24 and moved for divided argument, respondent-side amici (21 states, Chamber of Commerce, school-board groups) filed the same day, and argument is set for 2026-11-30. No disposition exists; nothing outcome-revealing was seen. The SG's side-switch (from supporting employee suits in Lakoski/Doe v. Mercy to supporting respondents here) was a material input to the forecast and is recorded in reasoning.md.

Forward cell; retrieval surfaced this docket's own post-cutoff filings (the United States' merits amicus brief supporting respondent and the Chamber/INGAA briefs, all filed 2026-09-21, and the 2026-11-09 argument setting). No disposition exists; the SG's merits-stage support for respondent, confirming the position its cert-stage CVSG brief already took, was a material input to the forecast. Disclosed as hygiene, not as a breach.
Encountered CourtListener HTTP 429 rate limit during lower court decision search; degraded gracefully to provisioned QPs and snapshot alone.

The provisioned petition and QP text are readable, but the separately linked appendix and docketed August 14 supplemental brief are not provisioned as text. No BIO text is supplied or BIO entry shown. The forecast relies on the petitioner's description of the lower-court orders and cannot independently assess the show-cause order or any supplemental argument. Prediction completed conservatively; no case outcome was sought or encountered.

The snapshot records an August 14 Brief for the Federal Respondents and September 1 reply, but the provisioned document manifest contains only the petition and QP. I retrieved those exact pre-decision PDFs from their snapshot links. The response materially changes the forecast: it requests a hold for McNutt and says the government no longer advances the commerce-power theory here. This gap was repaired for this prediction; no outcome or subsequent history was retrieved. Consider coverage of federal responses not titled brief in opposition.

Decisive forward-mode signal outside the provisioned inputs: the Solicitor General filed a companion petition from the Fifth Circuit's contrary decision (Department of Justice v. McNutt, No. 26-204, docketed Aug. 18, 2026), distributed for the same Oct. 9, 2026 conference, and asked the Court to grant McNutt and hold this petition. Both sides agree review is warranted. All of this predates the snapshot and is public; no disposition of this petition was sought or seen.

The document pipeline provisioned only petition.txt and questions-presented.txt. The respondents' filing on this docket is titled 'Brief for the Federal Respondents' (Aug. 14, 2026) rather than 'Brief in opposition', and no brief-in-opposition.txt was provisioned; I retrieved and read it from supremecourt.gov. The BIO fetcher may be missing the government's response-brief caption.

The most likely path is a hold pending No. 26-204, so this event may not resolve until McNutt is decided (likely by late June 2027). A hold that ends in a GVR counts as a grant on the binary axis and a hold that ends in a denial does not; the probability stated is a mixture over those paths, not a forecast of the Oct. 9 conference alone.

External precedent verification was unavailable: the CourtListener Axon citation search returned HTTP 429 and web attempts returned no usable material. Prediction completed from the provisioned snapshot, petition, opposition, QPs, and committed statpack. No direct REST fallback or outcome retrieval occurred. The reply and amicus are docketed but their texts were not provisioned or retrieved.
